title: What If There Was A Package Manager For Coding Agent Skills?
description:
Skills are meant to be reusable… so why are they such a mess to manage?

If you’ve ever copied skill folders between repos, duplicated markdown files, or dealt with stale skills scattered across projects, this conversation will feel very familiar.

In this video, we unpack a core irony of agent skills:
they’re designed for reuse, but until now, they’ve had no real distribution system.

That’s exactly the problem Tessl set out to solve.

🚀 What you’ll learn in this video:

Why skill sprawl happens across repos and teams

Why copying skills is a dead end for serious agent development

How Tessl brings proven software concepts—package management, versioning, and manifests—to agent skills

How to install, track, update, and manage skills without duplication

How to discover higher-quality skills using built-in evaluations

📦 Tessl’s skill package manager works the way professional developers expect:

Install skills from GitHub via the Tessl registry

Maintain a manifest of what’s installed

Update and track skills over time

Share skills across teams with proper access controls

Publish your own skills and get automatic evaluations when you do

Whether you’re a heavy skill consumer or actively publishing skills for your team or the community, this video shows how to move from chaos to control.

👉 Explore the registry: https://tessl.io/registry

Discover skills, publish your own, and finally manage them like real software.
